title: .github/workflows/ci.yml may assert only causes it has established, and the lint gate must be able to fail on a defect in the web application
base_commit_note: Started on a5548830; main moved to 6b078c2e (PR #79) mid-slice and this branch was rebased. PR #79 touched agent-state and apps/api only -- .github/workflows/ci.yml is byte-identical at both commits (blob 319efabe), so control evidence gathered before the rebase exercises the same file that ships. agent-state/current_contract.json is SINGLE-SLOT and was taken wholesale rather than merged.
evaluation_level_rationale: Both defects are in the gates that decide what reaches main. The first is wrong in the ALARMING direction and has produced three false alarms on this project; the second is wrong in the REASSURING direction, which is worse, because a green tick nobody can make red is trusted. This repository exists to refuse unsupported claims that a service is free; a gate that certifies less than its name claims is the mechanism by which such a claim eventually ships.
objective: Two repairs in one file. (1) Stop the secret-scan step translating a detect-secrets-hook exit status into a cause the workflow has not established, following the design merged in PR #80 for scripts/check.ps1 and scripts/check.sh, and close the symmetric false-GREEN if it is reachable. (2) Make the Node lint gate able to fail on a defect in the web application, by running apps/web's own lint and format:check inside the existing web job added by PR #75.
measured_premise: REPORTED and CONFIRMED by reading: .github/workflows/ci.yml maps detect-secrets-hook exit 1 to the single sentence 'detect-secrets found a secret that is not in the baseline.' The same defect was repaired in the two local check scripts by PR #80 (merged, a5548830); CI runs on Linux, so the branch is still live there.

MEASURED on this host, independently of the slice that reported it, with detect-secrets 1.5.0 (the exact version ci.yml pins) invoked as 'python -m detect_secrets.pre_commit_hook' inside a REAL git repository, reading the hook's OUTPUT before interpreting any code: a planted random high-entropy string exits 1 and names the finding; a baseline modified but NOT staged exits 1 with the hook's own words 'Your baseline file (.secrets.baseline) is unstaged.' and no secret anywhere; an invalid --baseline path exits 2. Exit 1 is therefore many-to-one with causes, by two separately produced instances.
MEASURED: 'detect-secrets-hook --baseline .secrets.baseline' with ZERO filenames exits 0 and prints NOTHING AT ALL. Silent success is the worst available shape for that condition.

MEASURED under the exact shell GitHub Actions uses for 'shell: bash' (bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail): an empty bash array expands to ZERO arguments (argc=0) because nounset is off; and a FAILING command inside a process substitution does NOT abort the script under errexit, leaving files=() silently. errexit was confirmed ON in-process via $- = 'ehB' and 'shopt -o errexit'. The step's own echo of the file count would print 'Scanning 0 tracked file(s).' and nothing asserts on it. The false GREEN is therefore STRUCTURALLY REACHABLE in ci.yml and is closed by this slice.

REPORTED by two independent slices and CONFIRMED by reading: root eslint.config.js sets ignores including 'apps/web/' and root .prettierignore contains 'apps/web/'; apps/web declares its own lint and format:check scripts; nothing in scripts/check.ps1, scripts/check.sh or .github/workflows/ci.yml invokes them. ci.yml's node job runs 'npm run lint' at the repository ROOT, which the reporting slice measured as exactly ONE linted file, eslint.config.js itself.

MEASURED on this host: this worktree has no node_modules at the root and none in apps/web, and this machine's npm registry is not the public default. Running npm ci locally would rewrite lockfile resolved URLs to an internal package-feed host and, if committed, leak internal infrastructure into a PUBLIC repository. The Node side is therefore verified by CI in a clean environment and NOT locally, deliberately.
in_scope: .github/workflows/ci.yml - the secrets job's 'Scan tracked files against baseline' step
.github/workflows/ci.yml - the web job, extended with apps/web's own ESLint and Prettier gates
.github/workflows/ci.yml - comments recording measured scope where a job name is broader than what it covers
out_of_scope_zero_diff: agent-state/feature_list.json - must stay byte-identical, verified by git hash-object. F008 stays passes:false.
package-lock.json and apps/web/package-lock.json - must stay BYTE-IDENTICAL to main, verified by blob hash. npm ci and npm audit fix are forbidden locally.

apps/web source and configuration - if apps/web lint or format:check fails on today's code, that is REPORTED, not fixed. Reformatting the application to make a new gate green would be a different and much larger change hiding inside a CI slice.
tests/support/source_scan.py and tests/unit/test_secrets_baseline.py - protected, must stay byte-identical. ci.yml is constrained by them and the constraints are preserved rather than relaxed.
apps/api/app/ingest/**, apps/api/app/read_api/** and tests under those areas - held by two concurrent slices in independent evaluation.

root eslint.config.js and .prettierignore - apps/web is excluded there BECAUSE it has its own tooling; the defect is that nothing invoked that tooling, not that the exclusion is wrong. Un-excluding it would lint TSX with a config that has no TypeScript parser.

job NAMES - branch protection requires check names, and ci.yml already records that a step was kept inside an existing job 'so the existing required check name is unchanged'. Renaming a job to describe its widened coverage would break a required check.
acceptance_criteria: AC1 - No branch of the secret-scan step states a cause the workflow has not established. The hook's own stdout and stderr are surfaced, and the reported status is the one actually observed.
AC2 - detect-secrets exit 1 no longer asserts that a secret was found.
AC3 - A baseline REWRITE is named only when established by comparing the bytes of .secrets.baseline before and after the hook runs, not inferred from exit code 3.
AC4 - An empty scan file list FAILS naming that as its cause, instead of passing having scanned nothing. The count is asserted against an impossible value (zero).
AC5 - Detection is preserved: a genuine finding still fails the step. The honest-cause change must not turn a real detection into a pass.
AC6 - The web job runs apps/web's own lint and format:check, so a lint defect in the web application can turn CI red.
AC7 - Each new gate is a step of its own and can be shown to fail INDIVIDUALLY, read at STEP level, with every other job green.
AC8 - The new gates do not redden the current tree. If they do, that is reported, not fixed.

AC9 - ci.yml remains accepted by tests/unit/test_secrets_baseline.py with that file and tests/support/source_scan.py unmodified: the NUL-delimited read, the ls-files -z enumeration, the literal quoted array argument and the file-count expansion all survive in an executed run body; no mapfile; no command-substituted ls-files on an executable line; exactly one check_secrets_baseline invocation, unconditional and at block depth 0.
AC10 - No check is weakened anywhere. No override, no suppression, no relaxed --audit-level, no registry bypass.
negative_and_regression_tests: BASELINE: the unmutated branch is GREEN and all five jobs ran BY NAME (python, node, web, secrets, dependencies). Absence of red is not evidence of green; the check-run count has a floor of 5.
RED-1 secret scan, detection direction: a planted random high-entropy string (never a credential, never a vendor example key) must turn the scan step RED, with the hook naming the finding.

RED-2 secret scan, impostor direction: an UNSTAGED .secrets.baseline must turn the step RED with the hook's own 'is unstaged' words and NO claim that a secret was found. On main's text the same condition announces a secret leak.
RED-3 empty file list: forcing zero enumerated files must turn the step RED naming the empty list, where today it prints 'Scanning 0 tracked file(s).' and passes.
RED-4 apps/web ESLint: a deliberate lint error under apps/web/src must turn the new ESLint step RED. The same error at repository root today is invisible to the web application.
RED-5 apps/web Prettier: a deliberate formatting violation under apps/web must turn the new format:check step RED.

Each RED case: predicted BEFORE the run, read at STEP level not job level, every other job green, then restored and proven byte-identical by git hash-object AND raw byte comparison. Never git diff --numstat.
Each mutation: anchor asserted to match EXACTLY ONCE and the patched line printed. A mutation that does not apply looks exactly like a control that does not fire.
verification_commands: python yaml.safe_load over .github/workflows/ci.yml - the file still parses and the step list is what it claims
gh run view --json jobs - step-level conclusions, asserted by NAME
git hash-object on every protected path, compared against origin/main
raw byte prefix comparison for agent-state/progress.md append-only proof
data_security_privacy_portability_z0: No product behaviour changes. No Z0 rule, quota, classification, schema, migration, endpoint or dependency is touched. No new network access. No credential, registry URL or internal package-feed hostname may reach any file, log, report, commit message or PR body. The planted proof string is randomly generated at use time and is not a credential of any kind. Portability unchanged: the step remains POSIX-shell and adds no tool beyond cmp, mktemp and sed, all of which the step's sibling in scripts/check.sh already relies on.
boundary: Draft PR only. Do not merge. Do not flip any ledger flag. Do not modify agent-state/feature_list.json.
